cues.en: If you get hold of two magnets and you push them, you can feel this pushing between them. Turn it around the other way and it... And they slam together. Now, what is it, the feeling between those two magnets?
cues.zh: 如果你拿两块磁铁，把它们往一起推，你能感觉到它们之间有股推力。把它转个方向，然后它……它们会啪地吸在一起。那么，这两块磁铁之间的那种感觉，到底是什么？

cues.en: What do you mean what's the feeling between the two magnets? There's something there, isn't there? I mean, that the sensation is that there's something there when you push these two magnets together. Listen to my question. What is the meaning when you say that there's that there's a feeling? Of course, you feel it. Now, what do you wanna know?
cues.zh: 你问两块磁铁之间那种感觉是什么，是什么意思？那里确实有某种东西，对吧？我是说，你把两块磁铁往一起推时，感觉上就是那里有某种东西。听我的问题。你说那里有一种感觉，这是什么意思？你当然能感觉到它。那你想知道的是什么？

cues.en: What I want to know is what's going on.
cues.zh: 我想知道的是，到底发生了什么。

cues.en: The magics repel
cues.zh: 磁铁会排斥

cues.en: repel each other. And, well, then what does that... But what does that mean? Or why are they doing that? Or how are they doing it?
cues.zh: 互相排斥。那么，这……但这意味着什么？或者它们为什么这么做？又或者它们是怎么做到的？

cues.en: You're asking... I must say, I think that's a perfectly reasonable question. Of course, are It's an excellent question.
cues.zh: 你是在问……我得说，我认为这是个完全合理的问题。当然，这是个极好的问题。

cues.en: Okay?
cues.zh: 好吧？

cues.en: But the problem that you are asking, you see, when you ask why something happens,
cues.zh: 但你看，你问的问题在于：当你问一件事为什么会发生时，

cues.en: how does a person answer why something happens?
cues.zh: 一个人该怎么回答“一件事为什么会发生”呢？

cues.en: For example,
cues.zh: 比如说，

cues.en: aunt Minnie is in a hospital. Why?
cues.zh: Minnie 阿姨住院了。为什么？

cues.en: Because she slipped. She went out and she slipped on the ice and broke her hip.
cues.zh: 因为她滑倒了。她出门，在冰上滑倒，摔断了髋骨。

cues.en: That satisfies people.
cues.zh: 这就能让人满意了。

cues.en: It satisfies, but it wouldn't satisfy someone who came from another planet, knew nothing about things. First you should understand why when you break your hip, do you go to the hospital?
cues.zh: 这能让人满意，但满足不了一个从另一个星球来、对世事一无所知的人。首先你得明白：为什么你摔断髋骨后，要去医院？

cues.en: How do you get to the hospital when the when the hip was broken? Well, because her husband seeing that she had the hip was broken, called the hospital up and sent somebody to get her. All that is understood by people.
cues.zh: 髋骨断了，你怎么到医院去呢？因为她丈夫看到她髋骨断了，就打电话叫医院，派人来接她。这些人们都能理解。

cues.en: Now when you explain a a why,
cues.zh: 现在，当你解释一个“为什么”时，

cues.en: you have to be in some framework that you allow something to be true.
cues.zh: 你必须处在某个框架里，允许某些事情为真。

cues.en: Otherwise, you're perpetually asking why. Why did the husband call up the hospital?
cues.zh: 否则，你就会无休止地问为什么。为什么丈夫要打电话叫医院？

cues.en: Because husband
cues.zh: 因为丈夫

cues.en: is interested in his wife's welfare.
cues.zh: 关心妻子的福祉。

cues.en: Not always. Some husbands aren't interested in their wife's welfare when they're drunk and they're angry.
cues.zh: 也不总是这样。有些丈夫喝醉了、发怒时，并不关心妻子的福祉。

cues.en: And so you begin to get a very interesting understanding of the world and all its complications.
cues.zh: 于是，你开始对这个世界及其所有复杂性，获得一种非常有趣的理解。

cues.en: In order to to... If you try to follow anything up,
cues.zh: 为了……如果你试着追问任何一件事，

cues.en: you go deeper and deeper in various directions.
cues.zh: 你就会朝各个方向越挖越深。

cues.en: If... For example, you could go, why did she slip on the ice? Well, ice is slippery. Everybody knows that. No problem.
cues.zh: 如果……比如，你可以问：她为什么会在冰上滑倒？嗯，冰很滑，大家都知道，没问题。

cues.en: But you ask, why is ice slippery?
cues.zh: 但你还要问：冰为什么滑？

cues.en: That's kinda curious. Ice is extremely slippery. It's very interesting.
cues.zh: 这就有点意思了。冰极其滑，这非常有趣。

cues.en: You say, how does it work? You could... You see, you could either say, I'm satisfied that you've answered me. Ice is slippery. That explains it. Or you could go on and say, why is ice slippery?
cues.zh: 你说，它是怎么回事？你可以……你看，你可以要么说：你的回答让我满意了。冰很滑，这就解释了。要么你可以继续问：冰为什么滑？

cues.en: And then you're involved with something because there aren't many things as slippery as ice. It's very hard to get greasy
cues.zh: 然后你就卷进某个问题里了，因为没多少东西像冰那么滑。很难找到那种油乎乎的

cues.en: stuff, but that's sort of wet and slimy.
cues.zh: 东西，但那是有点湿、黏糊糊的。

cues.en: But a solid that's so slippery?
cues.zh: 但一块固体怎么会这么滑？

cues.en: Because it is in the case of ice that when you stand on it, they say, momentarily the pressure melts the ice a little bit, so you got a sort of instantaneous
cues.zh: 因为就冰来说，据说你站在上面时，压力会瞬间把冰融化一点，于是你就有了一种瞬间的

cues.en: water surface on which you're slipping.
cues.zh: 水面，让你在上面打滑。

cues.en: Why on ice and not on other things? Because ice expands when it... Water expands when it freezes so the pressure tries to undo the expansion and melts it. It's capable of melting it. But other substances contract
cues.zh: 为什么是冰而不是别的东西？因为冰会膨胀，当它……水结冰时会膨胀，所以压力试图抵消这种膨胀并把它融化。压力确实能融化它。但其他物质会收缩

cues.en: when they're freezing and when you push them they're just satisfied
cues.zh: 当它们冻结时，你推它们，它们就甘于

cues.en: to be solid.
cues.zh: 保持固态。

cues.en: Why does water expand when it freezes and other substance don't expand when they freeze? Alright. I'm I'm not answering your question, but I'm telling you how difficult the why question is. You have to know what it is
cues.zh: 为什么水结冰时膨胀，而其他物质不膨胀？好吧。我不是在回答你的问题，而是在告诉你“为什么”这个问题有多难。你得知道它是什么——

cues.en: that you're permitted to understand
cues.zh: 哪些是你被允许理解的

cues.en: and allow to be understood and known and what it is you're not.
cues.zh: 以及哪些可以让你理解、认识和知道，哪些又不是。

cues.en: You'll notice in this example that the more I ask why,
cues.zh: 你会注意到，在这个例子里，我越问为什么，

cues.en: it gets interesting after that. It's my idea that the deeper a thing is the more interesting it is.
cues.zh: 之后就越有意思。我的想法是，一件事越深，就越有意思。

cues.en: And,
cues.zh: 而且，

cues.en: we could even go further and say, why did she fall down when she slipped? That has to do with gravity. Involves in all the planets and everything else. Never mind. It goes on and on. Now, when you ask for example,
cues.zh: 我们甚至可以更进一步说，她滑倒时为什么会摔倒？这和引力有关。涉及所有行星等等。别管了。它会一直追问下去。现在，比如你问，

cues.en: why two magnets repel,
cues.zh: 为什么两块磁铁相斥，

cues.en: there are many different levels. It depends on whether you're a student of physics or an ordinary person that doesn't know anything or not. If you're somebody who doesn't know anything at all about it, all I can say is that there is a magnetic force that makes them repel
cues.zh: 这里有很多不同层次。这取决于你是学物理的学生，还是什么都不知道的普通人。如果你对这事一无所知，我只能说，有一种磁力让它们相斥

cues.en: and that you're feeling that force.
cues.zh: 而你能感受到那种力。

cues.en: You see, but that's very strange because I don't feel kind of force like that in other circumstances.
cues.zh: 你看，但这很奇怪，因为我在别的情况下感觉不到那种力。

cues.en: When you turn them the other way, they attract.
cues.zh: 你把它们换个方向，它们就相吸。

cues.en: There's a very analogous force, electrical force, is which the same kind of a question. And you say that's also very weird.
cues.zh: 有一种非常类似的力——电力，它也是同一类问题。而你会说，那也很怪。

cues.en: But you're not at all disturbed by the fact that when you put your hand on the chair, it pushes you back.
cues.zh: 但你完全不会因为把手放在椅子上、椅子把你推回来而不安。

cues.en: But we found out by looking at it that that's the same force as a matter of fact. The electrical force, not magnetic exactly in that case. But it's the same electrical repulsions that are involved in keeping
cues.zh: 但仔细观察后我们发现，事实上那是同一种力。是电力，严格来说在这种情况下不是磁力。但正是同样的电斥力在阻止

cues.en: your finger away from the chair because everything's made out of its electrical forces in minor in microscopic details
cues.zh: 你的手指靠近椅子，因为在微观细节上，一切都是由电力构成的

cues.en: There's other forces involved, this is connected
cues.zh: 还涉及其他力，这和

cues.en: to electrical forces it turns out that the magnetic and the electric force with which I wish to explain these things this this repulsion in the first place is what ultimately is the deeper
cues.zh: 电力有关。结果发现，我最初想用来解释这些现象的磁力和电力，也就是这种斥力，最终才是更深的

cues.en: thing that we have to start that we can start with to explain many other things that looked like they were everybody would just accept them. You know you can't put your hand through the chair
cues.zh: 东西，是我们必须、也是可以拿来解释许多其他现象的东西——那些现象看起来人人都理所当然地接受。你知道，你不能把手穿过椅子

cues.en: that's taken for granted
cues.zh: 这是理所当然的

cues.en: but that you can't put your hand through the chair when looked at more closely why
cues.zh: 但更仔细地看，为什么你不能把手穿过椅子

cues.en: it involves the same repulsive forces
cues.zh: 这涉及同样的斥力

cues.en: that appear in magnets.
cues.zh: 也就是磁铁中出现的斥力。

cues.en: The situation you then have to explain is why in magnets it goes over a bigger distance than in ordinarily.
cues.zh: 那么你需要解释的，就是为什么磁铁的作用距离比平时要远得多。

cues.en: And there it has to do with the fact that in iron all the electrons are spinning in the same direction. They all get lined up and they magnify the effect of the force until it's large enough at a distance that you can feel it
cues.zh: 这跟铁原子里的电子都朝同一方向自旋有关。它们排列整齐，放大了力的效应，直到在较远距离上大到能被你感受到，

cues.en: but it's a force which is present all the time and very common and is in a basic force of almost I mean I can go a little further back if I were more technical
cues.zh: 但这种力其实一直存在，而且非常普遍，几乎是一种基本力——如果讲得更专业点，我还可以往更深处讲，

cues.en: But in the early level I've just have to have to tell you that's gonna be one of the things you'll just have to take as an element in the world the existence of magnetic repulsion or electrical
cues.zh: 但在入门层面上，我只能告诉你，有些东西你只能当作世界的基本要素来接受，比如磁斥力或者电……

cues.en: or electrical attraction, magnetic attraction.
cues.zh: 或者电引力、磁引力的存在。

cues.en: I can't explain that attraction in terms of anything else that's familiar to you.
cues.zh: 我无法用你熟悉的任何其他事物来解释这种吸引力。

cues.en: For example, if we say the magnets attract like as if they were connected by rubber bands, I would be cheating you
cues.zh: 比如，要是说磁铁相吸就像是用橡皮筋连在一起，那我就是在糊弄你，

cues.en: because they're not connected by rubber bands. I shouldn't be in trouble.
cues.zh: 因为它们根本没连着橡皮筋。这会让我自找麻烦。

cues.en: You'd soon ask me about the nature of the bands.
cues.zh: 你很快就会问我橡皮筋的本质是什么。

cues.en: And secondly,
cues.zh: 其次，

cues.en: if you were curious enough, you'd ask me why rubber bands tend to pull back together again and I would end up explaining that in terms of electrical forces,
cues.zh: 如果你足够好奇，还会问我为什么橡皮筋会缩回去，结果我最终又得用电力来解释，

cues.en: which are the very things that I'm trying to use the rubber bands to explain. So I have cheated very badly, you see.
cues.zh: 而电力恰恰是我试图用橡皮筋来解释的东西。所以你看，我这糊弄得太严重了。

cues.en: So I'm not going to be able to give you an answer to why magnets attract each other except to tell you that they do
cues.zh: 所以，关于磁铁为什么相互吸引，除了告诉你“它们就是会相吸”，我给不出别的答案，

cues.en: and to tell you that that's one of the elements in the world of different kinds of forces. There are electrical forces, magnetic forces, gravitational forces and others
cues.zh: 只能告诉你这是世界不同作用力中的基本要素之一。世界上有电力、磁力、引力等等，

cues.en: and those are some of the parts.
cues.zh: 这些就是世界的组成部分。

cues.en: If you were a student you go fur... I could go further. I could tell you that the magnetic forces are related to the electrical forces very intimately.
cues.zh: 如果你是专业学生，我还可以讲得更深一点。我可以告诉你，磁力和电力有着极其密切的联系，

cues.en: That our relationship between the gravity forces and electrical forces remains unknown
cues.zh: 而引力和电力之间的关系至今仍是未解之谜，

cues.en: and so on.
cues.zh: 诸如此类。

cues.en: But I really can't do a good job,
cues.zh: 但我实在没法很好地、

cues.en: any job,
cues.zh: 甚至根本没法，

cues.en: of explaining magnetic force in terms of something else that you're more familiar with because I don't understand it in terms of anything else that you're more familiar with.
cues.zh: 用你更熟悉的事物来解释磁力，因为我自己也无法用任何你更熟悉的东西去理解它。
